title: Characteristics of those who subject others to online hate in Australia
abstract: Online hate refers to hateful posts or comments about a person or group based on discrimination or bias related to their identity or beliefs. In late 2024, a survey of 9,951 Australian adults found 1.7 percent of respondents had subjected others to online hate. This study aimed to determine the characteristics of this cohort. Compared to those who had not subjected others to online hate, these respondents were more likely to be men, to be aged under 35 years and to be more impulsive. They were also more likely to have had previous negative life experiences (including victimisation to online hate), to hold prejudicial attitudes and to engage in a range of antisocial behaviours.
